_doc: THE CAST'S EMOTIONAL COVERAGE — the authoring input to tools/gen-cutin-art.mjs.
WHY THIS IS ONE FILE AND NOT 27. Every other per-character fact lives in
tools/characters/<id>.json, and this deliberately does not: the question this file
answers is a CAST question. 'Which of these people can smile, and which can only
scowl' is read across the whole town or not at all, and the coverage table the
user asked for is this file with a count next to each row. Identity still comes
from the per-character config (its sheetHint is the wardrobe line) and, far more
strongly, from the reference image; nothing here re-describes a face.
THE RULING THIS SERVES (user, 2026-08-01). The shipped portraits read 'emotionless
and dead'. Two things follow and both are in the data below. First, NO DEADPAN
NEUTRALS: `rest` is not 'no expression', it is the face this person wears when
nothing in particular is happening, and it has to carry who they are — docs/VOICES.md
is the authority for who that is, and every `rest` line below is written off that
entry. Second, EXPRESSIONS ARE PUSHED: a cut-in is read at a glance at ~500 px, so
each mood names a BROW, a MOUTH and a POSTURE rather than a feeling, because a
feeling is what the model averages away and a mouth shape is what it draws.
TIERS (the user's budget shape): `A` named story cast, 5-8 moods — vesper and lake
carry the most screen time in the game and get the fullest sets of anyone; `B`
chapter-2 cast and shopkeepers, 3; `C` archetypes, 2 — a market woman who can smile
and scowl beats seven of nobody.
SUPERSET RULE, and it is a hard one: every mood that already has cutin-<mood>.png
art, and every mood public/game/dialogue.json asks for, appears below. Dropping one
would silently demote a scripted line to the neutral plate, which is the regression
this whole lane exists to avoid. tools/gen-cutin-art.mjs --check asserts it.

`extra` is a per-character prompt clause, added for one reason and used sparingly: Lake's ratified bust is an airbrushed painting whose edges dissolve into a glow, and three rolls in a row reproduced that glow as background bloom the matte cannot key. A clause aimed at the one plate that needs it beats loosening the prompt for 138.

`gesture` is personality flavour for the prompt's POSE block, applied to NON-NEUTRAL plates only. USER RULING 2026-08-01 (suite v2 review): gesture direction approved, but a per-character MENU of hand moves repeated verbatim in every mood collapsed the suite into pointing/palming everywhere — so emotion-specific body language now lives IN each mood's own text (posture, lean, shoulder line, head angle; hands only where the pose calls for them, quiet on inward moods like sad/thinking), and `gesture` shrinks to how this person carries themselves. Vesper converted first; the REST OF THE CAST CONVERTED 2026-08-01 (rollout lane): every gesture line naming a held object (rowan's ledger, pell's wick-knife, sorrel's peel, creel's rope, tally's book, hobb's coil, odessa's rope/bowl, poppy's tray, finn's rope, pip's stick, eelwife's goods) rewritten to carriage-only. The earlier prop vocabulary (Rowan's ledger etc.) was already overruled: no props in moods, ever. `rest` stays exempt and composed.

vesper.rest: chin a little raised, one eyebrow fractionally higher than the other, the wry confident half-smile she wears while sizing something up — alert and amused, not warm

moods.happy: a real open grin, eyes crinkled almost shut — the unguarded one that escapes before she can file it; the whole body lifts with it, chest up, shoulders open and bright, head tipped back a little
moods.wry: one brow up hard, mouth pulled sideways into a dry flat line — deadpan disbelief; weight dropped onto one hip, head tipped back a fraction and turned a few degrees away while the eyes stay on you
moods.worried: the inner ends of both eyebrows RAISED and pulled upward together — the classic worry brow, never lowered, never a scowl — eyes wide and unsettled, glancing aside; lips pressed thin or bitten; anxious, apprehensive, the professional calm visibly cracking. This is FEAR-FOR-SOMEONE, not anger: nothing about the face is aggressive
moods.surprised: eyes wide, brows shot up, mouth open on a caught breath — the whole upper body rocked back from the waist, shoulders jumped, chin pulled in
moods.determined: firm, grounded resolve — eyes locked steadily on the person she is talking to, jaw set, mouth a firm straight line, head level and still; the quiet weight of a decision already made. Serious and immovable, with presence but NO heat: no smirk, no snarl, no blazing glare, no scowling brows — brows stay level; the intensity is in the stillness
moods.sad: eyes lowered and glassy, mouth small and unsteady — grief she would never name out loud; head dropped and turned a little aside, shoulders fallen, arms hanging still, hands quiet
moods.tender: her usual guard visibly DROPPED — and it should read like an event: head tipped, a real warm smile breaking through with a little helpless laugh in it, eyes bright and crinkled with open affection, maybe a hand loosely over her heart or tucking her braid back; the wry mapmaker caught actually caring and not managing to hide it — vivid, warm and unmistakably HER, never polite or neutral
moods.thinking: eyes up and off to one side, lips pressed into a working line, one brow raised — caught mid-calculation; chin lifted, torso turned a quarter away with the head tilting back toward you, still and self-contained, hands quiet
moods.annoyed: one brow cocked down while the other stays level, eyes half-lidded and flat, mouth pulled tight to one side in visible exasperation — irritated and unimpressed, done with this conversation but tolerating it; distinctly milder than anger, drier than worry

vesper.gesture: Vesper's body language is a mapmaker's — precise, economical, nothing wasted: most of what she feels reads in her spine, her chin and her shoulder line before her hands say anything, and when a hand does move it is deliberate and exact. USER RULING 2026-08-01: no notebook, no pencil, no held object in any mood — the emotion is played to her conversation partner, never to a prop.

lake.extra: This character's reference plate is a soft airbrushed painting that dissolves into a glow at its edges — three separate rolls reproduced that glow as a bloom in the background. Do not. Give him a hard clean edge with the background colour uniform right up to it, and no soft light of any kind around him.
lake.gesture: A lamplighter's manner: unhurried, careful, physically gentle, taking up little room. REDLINE — this character has ALREADY been drawn many times with one PALM TURNED OPEN AND RAISED toward the viewer and with a HAND LAID FLAT ON HIS OWN CHEST at the flame-pin. Those two hand poses are used up: do not draw either of them again. Put the acting somewhere else in the body — the tilt and turn of the head, the height and set of the shoulders, a lean in or away, the spine drawing up or slumping, arms folded, hands clasped low, one hand at his hip, an elbow tucked against the ribs, or both arms simply hanging quiet at his sides. Keep both hands LOW, below the collarbone, and well inside the frame.

rowan._hollow_red_2026_08_02: PARKED RED, and it blocks his whole new identity. rest/grave/happy/puzzled/tender all pass on the candidate-B art; `hollow` failed the straight-waist gate on THREE consecutive rolls (bot_cut 0.799 / 0.770 / 0.744 against the 0.80 floor, instrument tools/cutin_edge.py) so the atomic no-regression rule refused the set and his OLD-identity cut-ins still ship. Two things to know before spending another roll. FIRST, the gate number may be the wrong complaint: all three rolls raise a forearm across the chest, which lands inside the lower quarter that bot_cut divides by, so `lower` is inflated by a gesture rather than the last rows being narrow — the same class of failure cutin_edge's own history records for the `shoulder` statistic when arms are thrown open. MEASURE that before moving any threshold. SECOND, and independent of any gate: on the eye all three read as a warm engaged man with a raised palm, which is not 'the warm light gone out of him', and they are framed visibly tighter than his base plate. The mood text below plus this gesture line both push 'courteous', and the model is drawing the courtesy and dropping the emptiness — the likely fix is authoring (a hollow-specific text that says hands STILL and shoulders unmoved), not another roll of the same prompt.

moodDefaults._doc: SHARED DEFAULT MOOD TEXTS (user-ratified 2026-08-01, leaner scheme): a character entry uses these unless its own moods{} overrides the key. Encodes the facial-grammar lessons measured on Vesper: worried = inner brow ends RAISED (never knitted — that is the anger brow); determined = calm resolve with LEVEL brows (lowered brows read angry); tender = that character's guard visibly dropping, never generic softness. Overrides exist where a character demands more specificity — personality lives in the override, the rest text and the gesture line. | TIERED BUDGET (user 2026-08-01): only mainCharacters get the full default set; every other character inherits defaults ONLY for moods their dialogue actually uses (plus their own explicit overrides). Mains so far: vesper, lake, maren.
moodDefaults.happy: a real open smile breaking through, eyes lit and crinkled — unguarded, warm delight
moodDefaults.wry: one brow up, mouth pulled sideways into a dry knowing half-line — deadpan, amused, unimpressed
moodDefaults.worried: the inner ends of both eyebrows RAISED and drawn upward together — the worry brow, never lowered, never a scowl — eyes wide and unsettled, lips pressed thin; anxious fear-for-someone, nothing aggressive in the face
moodDefaults.surprised: eyes wide, brows shot up, mouth open on a caught breath, head pulled back a fraction
moodDefaults.determined: quiet unshakable resolve, NOT anger: chin lifted slightly, eyes steady with calm certainty, brows LEVEL — never lowered or knitted — mouth set in a small firm line; someone who has decided and cannot be talked out of it, composed rather than fierce
moodDefaults.sad: eyes lowered and glassy, mouth small and unsteady, the face fallen — grief held quietly
moodDefaults.tender: this character's usual guard visibly DROPPED, read as an event against their resting manner: real warmth breaking through, eyes bright with open affection, a genuine unguarded smile — vivid and personal, never polite or neutral
moodDefaults.thinking: eyes up and off to one side, lips pressed into a working line, one brow raised — caught mid-calculation
moodDefaults.annoyed: one brow cocked down while the other stays level, eyes half-lidded and flat, mouth pulled tight to one side in visible exasperation — irritated but tolerating it; milder than anger
